tasks.spec:
You are an Elixir/OTP engineer implementing one module in a real repository. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the Cornerman repo (an Elixir port of the Ringer agent-swarm tool). Edit files here directly.

NEVER TOUCH: anything under test/ (the tests are the acceptance check and are read-only), .git, any file outside the owned paths below. Do not git commit, do not push, do not run git add. Do not add or change dependencies: erlexec ~> 2.5 is already declared in mix.exs and is the mechanism to use.

OWNED PATHS (the only files you may create or edit): lib/cornerman/spawn.ex, anything under lib/cornerman/spawn/, lib/cornerman/application.ex, mix.exs (only if erlexec needs application config there), mix.lock (only if mix rewrites it), and ./notes.md.

GOAL: implement Cornerman.Spawn in lib/cornerman/spawn.ex so that every test in test/cornerman/spawn_test.exs passes. Read that test file first: its @moduledoc is the full contract, and the tests pin each behaviour. In short:
- Cornerman.Spawn.start(argv, opts) returns {:ok, ref}. The command runs in its OWN process group, with stdin connected to /dev/null (EOF for readers, not a closed descriptor) and stderr merged into stdout. Options: :cwd, :timeout_ms (default :infinity), :kill_grace_ms (default 2000) = delay between SIGTERM and SIGKILL of the group.
- The calling process receives {:cornerman_spawn, ref, {:data, binary}} as output arrives, then exactly one {:cornerman_spawn, ref, {:exit, reason}} where reason is {:status, integer}, :timeout or :stopped.
- Cornerman.Spawn.stop(ref) kills the whole group (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after the grace period) and returns :ok.
- The whole process group must die on timeout, on stop/1, when the Erlang process that called start/2 dies, and when the entire BEAM is killed with SIGKILL. Grandchildren that ignore SIGTERM must still die. Messages must go to the process that called start/2.
erlexec's source and docs are in deps/erlexec after the setup step (see src/exec.erl for options such as {group, 0}, kill_group, kill_timeout, stdout/stderr redirection and monitor). Keep the design small and idiomatic OTP; add a supervised process only if the behaviour needs one.

SETUP (run once, first, from this directory; the sandbox cannot fetch packages):
  cp -R /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/deps ./deps
  export PATH=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/elixir/1.20.1-otp-28/bin:/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/erlang/28.5/bin:$PATH HEX_OFFLINE=1

HOW TO RUN (after the setup, from this directory):
  mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix format
  mix test test/cornerman/spawn_test.exs
Iterate until all 11 tests pass. Your sandbox may restrict ps or signals in ways the real environment does not; if a test fails only for that reason, say so in notes.md. The verifying check runs outside your sandbox.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: lib/cornerman/spawn.ex implementing the contract, code formatted by mix format, compiling with no warnings, plus ./notes.md in this directory with: how the implementation maps each behaviour onto erlexec, anything you found surprising about erlexec, the test command output summary, and any test you believe is wrong (with the reason). Do not edit a test to make it pass.
